runs.name: normal-equation
runs.title: Closed-form solution
runs.description: Solves the least-squares problem exactly.

runs.name: gradient-descent
runs.title: Gradient descent
runs.description: Reaches the same solution iteratively. The loss curve shows convergence.

runs.name: high-noise
runs.title: High noise
runs.description: Quadruples the noise. The fit stays unbiased but R² falls.

runs.name: overlapping
runs.title: Overlapping classes
runs.description: Class means are close. Accuracy is capped by the overlap, not by the model.

runs.name: l2
runs.title: L2 regularisation
runs.description: A strong penalty shrinks the weights and softens the decision surface.

runs.name: kmeans-plusplus
runs.title: k-means++ initialisation
runs.command: uv run python -m mlc.examples.kmeans fit -k 3 --init kmeans++

runs.name: random-init
runs.title: Random initialisation
runs.description: Same data and k. Random starts can need more iterations or land in a worse optimum.
runs.command: uv run python -m mlc.examples.kmeans fit -k 3 --init random --seed 3

gradient-descent.title: Gradient descent and momentum in NumPy

runs.name: step-sizes
runs.title: Step size against the stability limit
runs.description: Four step sizes on linear regression, from 10% to 102% of 2/λ_max. The last one diverges.

runs.name: momentum
runs.title: Momentum on a narrow valley
runs.description: Plain gradient descent and heavy-ball momentum (β = 0.9) with the same step size and start.

runs.name: momentum-high-beta
runs.title: Too much momentum
runs.description: β = 0.99 overshoots the valley floor repeatedly. The loss rises and falls instead of decreasing.

gaussian-mixture-model.title: Gaussian mixture model (diagonal covariance) by EM in NumPy

runs.name: fit
runs.title: EM with k-means++ initialisation
runs.command: uv run python -m mlc.examples.gmm fit -k 3 --init kmeans++

runs.name: compare
runs.title: Gaussian mixture against k-means
runs.description: Same data, same k. k-means cuts the elongated clusters with straight boundaries; the mixture follows their shapes.

runs.name: select
runs.title: Choosing k with AIC and BIC
runs.description: The log-likelihood keeps rising with k. AIC and BIC add a penalty per parameter; BIC's grows with log n.

welch-t-test.title: Pooled and Welch t-tests in NumPy and SciPy

runs.name: compare
runs.title: Same data, two tests
runs.description: Equal true means: a large low-variance group against a small high-variance group. The pooled test rejects (p ≈ 0.03); Welch does not (p ≈ 0.21). About 1 draw in 20 disagrees like this at this setting.

runs.name: sweep
runs.title: Type I error across variance ratios
runs.description: With equal means, Welch stays near α everywhere. The pooled test drifts badly when the smaller group has the larger variance.

singular-value-decomposition.title: Truncated SVD and the Eckart–Young theorem in NumPy

runs.name: low-rank
runs.title: Low-rank approximation of a test image
runs.description: For every rank k, the spectral error equals σ_{k+1} and the Frobenius error equals the root sum of the discarded σᵢ², as Eckart–Young predicts.

linear-models.title: Linear models in scikit-learn on the diabetes data

runs.name: ols
runs.title: Ordinary least squares
runs.description: The unpenalised fit. s1 and s2, which are correlated at 0.9, get large coefficients of opposite sign.

runs.name: ridge
runs.title: Ridge
runs.description: An L2 penalty shrinks every coefficient and tames the s1/s2 pair, but zeroes none.

runs.name: lasso
runs.title: Lasso
runs.description: An L1 penalty sets some coefficients exactly to zero.

runs.name: elastic-net
runs.title: Elastic net
runs.description: Half L1, half L2: fewer zeros than the lasso, and correlated features share weight.

runs.name: lars
runs.title: Least-angle regression
runs.description: The whole LARS path and the order in which features enter.

runs.name: sgd-lasso
runs.title: SGD with an L1 penalty
runs.description: SGDRegressor approaches the exact lasso solution; the objective gap shrinks slowly with the epochs.
runs.command: uv run python -m mlc.examples.linear_models --model sgd --penalty l1 --alpha 1.0 --epochs 60

svm-solvers.title: A six-point soft-margin SVM, solved exactly

runs.name: quadratic-programme
runs.title: Quadratic programme by active sets
runs.description: Tries active sets until one satisfies every KKT condition, then recovers w, b and each slack.

runs.name: smo
runs.title: Sequential minimal optimisation
runs.description: Four SMO steps from α = 0 reach the same α, w, b and slacks in exact arithmetic.
